NAM.note: No exchange between civil register and ID system is described.
No count or share of people enrolled is stated.
The random number goes to first-time ID applicants, not to births.

facts.fact: The Office of the Prime Minister says it provides oversight, technology support, quality assurance and management of key components of the national population register on which the E-ID is built, and the Ministry of Home Affairs runs the existing registration infrastructure.

systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security; Office of the Prime Minister

facts.fact: The Office of the Prime Minister says electronic identity verification of social grant beneficiaries already prevents payments to deceased beneficiaries.
The Office of the Prime Minister says government has saved approximately N$16 million on social grants through improved identity verification.
Officials say E-ID smart cards with a chip holding biometric and biographical data, including fingerprints, will be rolled out from September 2026 to new applicants.
Existing identity cards stay legally valid until withdrawn by gazette, and the E-ID is built on the national population register.
